answer_1.quote: Given a source sentence s and a human-generated translation t, the goal of TEC is to produce a corrected target language sentence t'.

answer_2.quote: The primary metric for TEC is MaxMatch scores (M2) (Dahlmeier and Ng, 2012) computed with the errant toolkit. M2 is a standard metric for GEC that aligns t and t' to extract discrete 'edits.' ... We choose to follow the GEC evaluation practice of up-weighting precision by comparing F0.5 ... Next, we compare sentence-level accuracy ... We compute overall sentence-level accuracy ... We also report accuracy per error type ...

answer_4.quote: We ran a human-in-the-loop user study with nine professional translators using our best-performing TEC model. ... To evaluate whether TEC has an effect on quality, we asked a 10th translator to compare the quality of the reviewed sentences by ranking the 9 reviewed translations, with ties allowed.
answer_4.guideline: The translator was asked to compare the quality of the reviewed sentences by ranking the 9 reviewed translations, with ties allowed. The explicit goal is to ensure consistency with conventions in the training documents.
